bio: Tonga's second-largest town, a sheltered harbour base for sailing, whale tours and island trips.
Neiafu is the main town of Vavaʻu, set on the Port of Refuge harbour, with the boats, cafés and tours.
The harbour town where most Vavaʻu visits start, with around 3,800 residents on the Port of Refuge.
A sea cave reached by boat, entered through an underwater tunnel, on day trips around the Vavaʻu islands.
Reached by boat, this Vavaʻu sea cave is entered by swimming through an underwater tunnel.
Boat trips from Neiafu visit this sea cave, whose entrance is an underwater tunnel.
A sea cave reached by boat from Neiafu, known as an excellent place to snorkel.
Reached only by boat, Swallows Cave is a Vavaʻu sea cave visited on day trips for its snorkelling.
Day boat trips from Neiafu stop at this cave, which is excellent for snorkelling.
An island 35 minutes by boat from Neiafu, with sheltered bays where humpback whales gather with their calves.
Reached by boat from Neiafu in about 35 minutes, Hunga Island has sheltered bays used by whales with calves.
Humpback whales gather around this island's sheltered bays each season, a short boat ride from Neiafu.
An island about five minutes by boat from Neiafu, with good beaches and snorkelling.
Vavaʻu's second-largest island, joined to ʻUtu Vavaʻu by a land bridge, with beaches and snorkelling.
A short boat ride from Neiafu brings you to beaches and snorkelling on this island.
A national park near Neiafu with a steep 10 to 20 minute climb to a lookout.
Mt Talau's short trail climbs steeply from an entrance about 2 km from Neiafu to a lookout.
Vavaʻu's national park, set up in 1995, has a steep 1 km trail up to a lookout.
Tonga's only botanical garden, in Tuʻanekivale village, visited on guided tours with tapa-making and kava.
A botanical garden on Vavaʻu's east coast with the largest plant collection in Tonga, visited by guided tour.
Tonga's largest plant collection, on Vavaʻu's east coast, with a visitors' centre showing tapa-making and kava.
